ceramic.snippet:
Crude and natural gas prices strengthened in the first quarter. ExxonMobil’s crude realizations were impacted by an increased discount in Western Canada, notably for heavy crudes, as Canadian supply exceeded pipeline and rail capacity.

  ExxonMobil announced its seventh oil discovery offshore Guyana with the completion of the Pacora-1 exploration well. The well encountered approximately 65 feet (20 meters) of high-quality, oil-bearing sandstone reservoir.  During the quarter, the company increased its holdings in Brazil’s pre-salt basins after winning eight additional exploration blocks, six of them to be operated by ExxonMobil, during the latest bid round. The company added more than 640,000 net acres to its existing deepwater portfolio offshore Brazil, and is now one of the largest acreage holders among international oil companies in the country.  ExxonMobil announced that its estimate of the size of the natural gas resource at the P’nyang field in Papua New Guinea (PNG) has increased to 4.36 trillion cubic feet of gas, an 84 percent increase from the previous assessment completed in 2012. This increase, based on an independent recertification study, supports a potential three-train expansion concept of the PNG LNG plant.  ExxonMobil sold its 50 percent ownership interest in the Scarborough gas field, offshore Western Australia, to Woodside Petroleum Ltd. In the Downstream, the company closed several divestments, including distribution and marketing assets in South America, and retail sites in Europe.  During the quarter, ExxonMobil added to its exploration portfolio offshore West Africa by signing an agreement with the government of Ghana to acquire exploration and production rights for the Deepwater Cape Three Points block. ExxonMobil also signed an agreement with a subsidiary of Galp Energia, SGPS, S.A. for a 40 percent farm-in to a deepwater license offshore Namibia. Both agreements are subject to government approvals.

Accounting for estimated timing effects:

Physical shipments of hydrocarbons and finished products are often hedged using financial derivatives in the normal course of business. At the

end of each quarter, accounting standards require open financial derivatives to be marked to current period-end prices (typically referred to as

“mark to market”) with the corresponding value reflected in current period earnings. The associated physical shipments are not marked to current

period-end prices but valued on the balance sheet in inventory primarily based on LIFO accounting rules. As a result, unlike the financial

derivatives, the value of the physical shipment is not reflected in earnings until the transaction is complete. This mismatch between the valuation

of the financial derivatives and the associated physical transaction results in a timing difference in earnings that unwinds over subsequent

quarters consistently delivering a net profit. LIFO valuation also drives timing differences between the accounting recognition of the settlement of

the derivatives and their offsetting physical shipments. Together, these are referred to as timing effects.

In periods of rising prices, the timing effects are typically negative, while in periods of decreasing prices, the timing effects are typically positive.

Importantly, excluding timing impacts, these trading and optimization activities have consistently delivered positive earnings to the Company.

Crude and products trading activity, which accounted for the majority of timing impacts in the third quarter, is included in the Energy Products

segment. Natural gas related impacts are included in the Upstream segment.

The company's performance was bolstered by strategic refinery reconfigurations on the U.S. Gulf Coast, which tripled energy products unit earnings per barrel since 2019 by increasing distillate yields. Management emphasized a commitment to shareholder returns, announcing an annual dividend increase and a plan to maintain $20 billion in yearly share buybacks through 2027. Additionally, the company has achieved $16.9 billion in cumulative structural cost savings since 2019, aiming for $20 billion by 2030 through centralized technology and operational efficiencies.

octen.title: ExxonMobil Holdings Corp (XOM) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Highlights:
octen.snippet:
Release Date: October 30, 2026
For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.
Positive Points
- ExxonMobil Holdings Corp XOM reported strong financial results with $15.4 billion in GAAP earnings and $25.7 billion in cash flow from operations for the quarter.
- The company increased its dividend per share by 4%, marking the 44th consecutive year of annual dividend growth, and plans to maintain $20 billion in share repurchases in 2027.
- ExxonMobil Holdings Corp (XOM) achieved record global refining utilization, excluding Middle East impacts, and industry-leading diesel production of 1.1 million barrels per day, helping to meet market demand.
- The company is advancing advantaged projects in Guyana, where production surpassed 1 billion barrels, and in LNG with the Uaru development and Mozambique's Rovuma project, expected to drive future growth.
- ExxonMobil Holdings Corp (XOM) realized $16.9 billion in structural cost savings since 2019 and is on track to reach $20 billion by 2030, improving efficiency and competitiveness.
Negative Points
- ExxonMobil Holdings Corp (XOM) faced ongoing volume impacts from Middle East conflicts, with a 350 KBD impact in the fourth quarter due to damaged LNG trains in Qatar and deferred sales in the UAE.
- The company experienced technical difficulties during the earnings call, which disrupted the presentation and may have affected communication clarity.
- ExxonMobil Holdings Corp (XOM) does not plan to host a formal corporate plan update event in December, potentially reducing transparency on long-term strategy.

octen.title: ExxonMobil Guides to Up to $4.2B Margin Lift in 3Q26, Flags $2.5B Timing Drag – Minichart
octen.snippet:
ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation (NYSE: XOM) told investors Friday that 3Q 2026 results should include a large sequential margin tailwind, partly offset by Middle East-linked timing and external headwinds, ahead of its October 30 earnings release.
The guidance, furnished in an 8-K under Item 7.01 (Regulation FD) and Exhibit 99.1, compares estimated 3Q26 factors with 2Q26 results. The company said the factors are limited in scope and are not an earnings estimate, but they give shareholders an early read on the quarter.
Margin Gains Lead, Timing Effects Cut the Other Way
ExxonMobil estimated the change in margins will add $4.5 billion in Energy Products, $0.5 billion in Specialty Products and $0.3 billion in Upstream, while Chemical Products margins are seen at negative $0.6 billion. The total estimated margin impact is a positive $4.4 billion.
That is partly offset by an estimated negative $2.5 billion in timing effects, which hit Energy Products at negative $1.9 billion and Upstream at negative $0.7 billion, with Chemical at negative $0.1 billion. The company attributed the drag to mark-to-market mismatches between derivatives and physical shipments, led by crude and products trading.
Prices, Volumes and Other Headwinds
- Liquids prices: negative $1.3 billion, all in Upstream.
- Gas prices: positive $0.3 billion in Upstream.
- Middle East volume disruption: $0.0 billion.

octen.title: ExxonMobil Stock Forecast: $4.5 Billion Refining Windfall Puts XOM at $179 Before Q3 Earnings
octen.snippet:
TradingKey - ExxonMobil (NYSE: XOM) closed at $178.98 on Friday, October 16, up 2.46% from Thursday. It is currently up about 49% in 2026, and Brent crude closed at $109.86 the same day as the attacks in the Strait of Hormuz escalated.
My thesis is that Exxon is going to have a strong Q3, likely from refining as opposed to crude. The main uncertainty is how long will the disruption in the Middle East keep margins elevated. The catalyst is confirmed: Exxon will report its Q3 results at 5:30 a.m. CT on Friday, October 30, and will hold an earnings call at 8:30 a.m. CT.
On October 16, Exxon provided an advance preview of “market and other factors” impacting Q3 results, relative to Q2. The company states it is not an earnings estimate, and excludes operating performance.
Refining continues to be the primary driver. Energy Products margins are estimated to be approximately $4.5 billion. Specialty Products margins are estimated to be about $0.5 billion and Chemical Products margins are estimated to subtract about $0.6 billion. In the Upstream, lower liquids prices are estimated to negatively impact margins by approximately $1.3 billion, while higher gas prices add approximately $0.3 billion.
Planned and other factors, including maintenance, external operational impacts, extra days and approximately $0.9 billion of Upstream entitlements, timing and tax, are estimated to negatively impact results by approximately $1.

octen.title: XOM: Refining Strength Holds Up, Relative Upside Looks More Constrained
octen.snippet:
What’s in the News for ExxonMobil Holdings
- ExxonMobil reported third quarter 2026 net income of US$15.4b and adjusted earnings per share of US$4.23, which surpassed analyst estimates, supported by full refinery utilization, elevated oil prices linked to the US Iran conflict, and upstream contributions from Guyana and the Permian Basin. Source: ExxonMobil and Chevron Report Record Q3 Profits Amid Refining Margin Surge and Geopolitical Tensions.
- Refining margins played a key role in recent results. ExxonMobil flagged a US$4.4b to US$4.5b uplift to third quarter earnings tied mainly to higher refining margins in its Energy Products segment, alongside a US$1.3b headwind from lower liquids prices and a US$300m gain from gas prices. Source: ExxonMobil Reports US$4.5 Billion Q3 Earnings Boost from Higher Refining Margins Amid Mixed Upstream Results.
- Dividend income remains an active part of the ExxonMobil story. The company declared a fourth quarter 2026 dividend of US$1.07 per share, payable on December 10, 2026, to shareholders of record on November 16, 2026, following an earlier dividend increase referenced in recent earnings coverage. Source: Key Developments and ExxonMobil and Chevron Report Record Q3 Profits Amid Refining Margin Surge and Geopolitical Tensions.
- Capital returns feature alongside earnings in recent updates. ExxonMobil announced a planned US$20b share repurchase program for 2027 and referenced continued focus on debt reduction and dividends, set against what management describes as market uncertainty and strong refining conditions.

seltz.snippet:
Accounting for estimated timing effects:

Physical shipments of hydrocarbons and finished products are often hedged using financial derivatives in the normal course of business. At the

end of each quarter, accounting standards require open financial derivatives to be marked to current period-end prices (typically referred to as

“mark to market”) with the corresponding value reflected in current period earnings. The associated physical shipments are not marked to current

period-end prices but valued on the balance sheet in inventory primarily based on LIFO accounting rules. As a result, unlike the financial

derivatives, the value of the physical shipment is not reflected in earnings until the transaction is complete. This mismatch between the valuation

of the financial derivatives and the associated physical transaction results in a timing difference in earnings that unwinds over subsequent

quarters consistently delivering a net profit. LIFO valuation also drives timing differences between the accounting recognition of the settlement of

the derivatives and their offsetting physical shipments. Together, these are referred to as timing effects.

In periods of rising prices, the timing effects are typically negative, while in periods of decreasing prices, the timing effects are typically positive.

Importantly, excluding timing impacts, these trading and optimization activities have consistently delivered positive earnings to the Company.

Crude and products trading activity, which accounted for the majority of timing impacts in the third quarter, is included in the Energy Products

segment. Natural gas related impacts are included in the Upstream segment.

### Key Terms

adjusted eps financial

Adjusted earnings per share (adjusted eps) is a measure of a company's profit per share that has been modified to exclude certain one-time or unusual items, such as costs from restructuring or asset sales. It provides a clearer picture of the company’s core performance by removing events that may distort the usual earnings. Investors use adjusted eps to better understand a company's ongoing profitability and compare it more accurately over time.

free cash flow financial

Free cash flow is the amount of money a company has left over after paying all its expenses and investing in its business, like buying equipment or updating facilities. It shows how much cash is available to reward shareholders, pay down debt, or save for future growth. This helps investors understand if a company is financially healthy and able to grow.

cagr financial

Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) measures the average yearly growth of an investment, revenue, or other metric over a multi-year period as if it had grown at a steady rate each year. Think of it like the constant speed that would take you from the starting value to the ending value over the same time—useful because it smooths out ups and downs and lets investors compare different assets or performance periods on an even footing.

fpso technical

A FPSO (Floating Production, Storage and Offloading unit) is a ship-like facility that sits offshore to process oil or gas pumped up from under the seabed, store the product, and transfer it to tankers or pipelines. For investors it matters because an FPSO turns remote reserves into cash: it represents a major capital asset and source of revenue but also concentrates operational, maintenance and safety risks that can affect production levels, costs and company valuation.
